Research interests

How green spaces shape a city’s carbon balance

I bring together field inventories, carbon accounting, spatial analysis, and interpretable machine learning to study how much carbon urban vegetation takes up and how much greenhouse gas its maintenance emits.

Street-level carbon accounting

In central Luohe, I compare annual vegetation carbon sequestration with emissions from green space maintenance. Mapping the net balance helps identify streets where changes in planting or care could have the most impact.

i-Tree Eco · ArcGIS Pro

Interpretable machine learning

I examine how vegetation structure, landscape configuration, and maintenance relate to carbon outcomes across street types. I’m particularly interested in how modeled outcomes change as irrigation and fertilizer inputs vary.

K-means · XGBoost · SHAP

Green infrastructure and park planning

Building on my Sponge City stormwater park research, I want to understand how connected street corridors and parks can support carbon sequestration, stormwater regulation, and public recreation.

Sponge City design · Urban park networks

Doctoral research

From roadside plots to a carbon map

I subtract maintenance emissions from i-Tree Eco sequestration estimates, map net carbon balance in ArcGIS Pro, and interpret drivers with XGBoost and SHAP.

  1. 01
    Inventory vegetation and maintenance

    Establish roadside plots and record vegetation, soil, and maintenance data across 117 streets in central Luohe.

  2. 02
    Estimate and map net carbon balance

    Compare annual vegetation carbon sequestration with estimated maintenance-related greenhouse gas emissions.

  3. 03
    Examine what drives the differences

    Compare street types to understand which planting and maintenance practices could improve their carbon balance.

Visiting scholar · 2024–2025

The Ohio State University

Columbus, Ohio

I worked with Prof. Qian (Victoria) Chen in the Department of Food, Agricultural and Biological Engineering on a regional green infrastructure assessment.

  • Modeling vegetation carbon

    I estimated how much carbon vegetation sequesters using i-Tree Eco and mapped the results in ArcGIS.

  • Mapping patterns in green space

    I processed field inventories and spatial data, calculated landscape metrics in FRAGSTATS, and used principal component analysis and K-means clustering in R to characterize green space patterns.
